title: Counting Bits
pattern: DP on bits: drop the last bit
statement: Given an integer `num`, return an array where entry `i` (for every `i` from 0 to `num`) is the **number of 1 bits** in the binary form of `i`.
idea: Counting the bits of each number separately works, but the numbers are closely related — reuse earlier answers.
Dropping the last binary digit of `i` gives `i // 2`, a **smaller** number whose bit count is already known.
The dropped digit is `i % 2`. So `bits(i) = bits(i // 2) + (i % 2)` — one lookup and one addition per number.

steps.text: Our example: **`num = 5`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
`bits_count[i]` will be the number of 1 bits in i. The number 0 has none, so `bits_count[0]` = 0 is already right.

views.title: bits_count[i] = number of 1 bits in i

steps.text: 1 is `0001`. Without its last bit it is `0000` = 0, which has 0 one-bits (already computed). The last bit is 1. So `bits_count[1]` = 0 + 1 = **1**.

steps.text: 2 is `0010`. Without its last bit it is `0001` = 1, which has 1 one-bit (already computed). The last bit is 0. So `bits_count[2]` = 1 + 0 = **1**.
